label: indices_reduced
label_description: Red-cell indices are reduced (MCH or MCV below the screening cut-off). Haemoglobin analysis and iron status are needed next. A CBC cannot say what the cause is.

trace.locator: s11.2 and s11.4: 99% of alpha-zero cases have MCH <25 pg; BSH-2023 PDF p.4 'If the MCH is <25 pg ... alpha-zero'
s1.1 Scenario 0 (MCH <27 pg -> HPLC or CE); TIF-OLD PDF p.21 and p.24 (MCV and/or MCH); SITE-2022 Recommendations (MCV <80 fL and MCH <27 pg in adults)

sources_disagree: MCV leg: NHS not used; TIF 79 (text) or 78 (flowchart); SITE 80.

sources.title: NHS England. Same handbook, chapter 'Antenatal screening' (sections 6.4 action values, 8 HbA2 problems, 9 iron deficiency, 10-11 alpha-zero, 12 risk assessment)
NHS England. Sickle cell and thalassaemia screening handbook for antenatal laboratories, 5th ed., chapter 'Interpretation and reporting of antenatal screening results'

not_a_diagnosis: This is a screening-support pattern for a clinician. It is not a diagnosis and not clinical advice. A CBC alone can never show whether someone carries a change; confirmation and interpretation belong to an accredited laboratory and a qualified clinician.
prior_art_note: Prior art: other public tools already interpret laboratory values (haemoglobin, MCV, MCH, HbA2, HbF, ferritin, G6PD) with named sources. This aid is not claimed as new; it is a closed-vocabulary, rule-traced aid in which every rule is gated on clinical sign-off.
population_caveat: The NHS and BSH rules were written for antenatal screening in England (high and low prevalence areas). Their use for non-pregnant premarital adults in the UAE is an extrapolation that the clinician must accept or reject explicitly.
